featured.title: Sam Altman · OpenAI CEO
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman posted two long threads laying out what "pacing the frontier" actually means. His core argument: frontier labs don't need to wait for an antitrust exemption or legislation to start building public confidence — the work starts now. He flagged a key shift: the old Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks focused mainly on deployment of finished models, not on what happens during development. OpenAI now formulates explicit safety cases *in advance* of frontier RL runs expected to…
featured.insightZh: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 这两天连发两条长文，第一次把「pacing（控速）」这个词摆到台面上讲清楚。他的核心论点是：前沿实验室不需要等反垄断豁免或立法落地才开始建立公众信心，现在就该做。他点名了一个关键转变——过去的 Responsible Scaling Policy 和 Preparedness Framework 主要管「模型发布之后」，而今天真正要管的是「开发过程本身」。OpenAI 现在的做法是：在启动那些预期会显著提升能力的前沿强化学习训练之前，就先写出明确的 safety case，而不只是发布前做安全评估。他同时划了两条绝对不能越过的红线：一是失去对未来的控制权（「我们毫无歉意地站在人类这一队」），二是权力过度集中——如果一个极度强大的 AI 被某一个人或一家公司用来把自己的世界观强加给所有人，结果会极度反乌托邦。他特别强调这里有个窄路要走：一个国家拿到过多权力是风险，一个实验室拿到过多权力同样是风险。最后他给「pacing」下了定义：pacing 不等于 stopping。进展会继续很快，但应该比它本可以达到的速度慢一些——safety case 和监控这些干预措施有实实在在的成本，但…

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie offered an enterprise-side read on the same pacing debate. He opened by conceding the word itself is a trigger — it sounds like an arbitrary slowdown of capability, or a way to hobble competitors through undue regulation. But he argues the specific improvement goals Dario laid out are absolute necessities in AI development, not optional extras. His reasoning is by analogy: we demand equivalent standards in aerospace, life sciences, and healthcare, so AI development likely shouldn't be different…
featured.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 对同一场 pacing 辩论给了一个更偏企业视角的判断。他先承认「pacing」这个词本身带触发性——听上去像是人为拖慢能力进展，或者用过度监管去阻碍竞争对手。但他认为 Dario 提出的那些具体改进目标是 AI 开发的绝对必需品，而不是可选项。他的论据是类比：航空航天、生命科学、医疗保健这些行业我们都要求等价的安全标准，AI 开发凭什么例外？尤其是当 AI 即将成为金融交易系统、医疗设备、生物技术突破、国防系统和政府工作流的底层技术时，要求这些系统安全且「对齐」完全说得通。他把真正的难题留在了最后：如何在不实质性拖慢创新进展、不减少竞争的前提下走到那一步，是 21 世纪最复杂的问题之一——但需求本身是真实存在的。

featured.title: Redefining Chip Architecture with Arm CEO Rene Haas
featured.summaryEn: Accelerators took all the attention, but something has to orchestrate and route the tokens the token factory produces — that's what CPUs do, and nothing has replaced them. Rene Haas runs ARM and SoftBank Group International. He joined ARM from Nvidia in 2013, and his first impression was "no inventory, no RMA, no scrap, what's not to like" — pure IP licensing at a 98.5% gross margin. Now ARM builds its own silicon, starting with a general-purpose agentic CPU for Meta, who came to them because "there wasn't anybody out who could give it to them." The move forced ARM to build supply chain operations, backend layout, implementation and bring-up labs from scratch. His read on AI in chip design is refreshingly specific: design cycles run 24–36 months, but the longest phase is not architecture or RTL generation — it's verification, validation, debug and documentation, which is exactly what AI…
featured.insightZh: 加速器抢走了所有注意力，但 token 工厂造出来的 token 得有人调度和分发——那是 CPU 的活，而 CPU 从来没有被替代过。 Rene Haas 是 ARM 的 CEO，同时管着软银集团国际业务。他 2013 年从英伟达加入 ARM，第一印象是「没有库存、没有退货、没有废料，这有什么不好的」——ARM 当时靠纯 IP 授权做到了 98.5% 的毛利率。而现在 ARM 自己下场造芯片了，第一个产品是给 Meta 做的通用 agentic CPU，因为「市场上没人能给他们」。这个转向需要 ARM 从零补上供应链运营、后端布局、实施、点亮实验室这些完全不同的肌肉。 他对 AI 改造芯片设计流程的判断非常具体：芯片设计周期是 24 到 36 个月，但耗时最长的环节不是架构设计和 RTL 生成，而是验证、确认、调试和文档——而 AI 恰好特别擅长这些。ARM 内部 80% 到 90% 的工程师现在每天都在用 AI。「如果我们把它关掉，就好比在 1990 年代，你有了互联网，然后你说只能在下午两点到四点之间上网，之后请去走廊尽头那个图书馆查书。会天下大乱。精灵已经出瓶了，没法收回去。」他也划了 AI 目前的能力边界：RTL 生成、物理设计和实现这三块工具还不够成熟，因为模型只能在公开数据上训练，而这些信息高度专有。他顺带讲了一个反直觉的观点——ARM 的护城河不只是 IP 本身，而是文档和测试台：「没有文档就不可用，不可测试；不可用不可测试就不可训练；不可训练就没法用 AI。」时间尺度上他不认同两三年内见效，但认为五到十年内「从想法直接生成 GDS II 文件」对于较直接的设计是完全可能的。 关于 AI 泡沫，他的区分很干脆：抛开估值泡沫（那是股市指数层面的事），如果问的是供给是否过剩于需求——「根本不接近」。他认为接下来的瓶颈会从封装、内存转移到数据中心建设本身，而且部分原因是政治性的：美国多地出现反数据中心的声浪。他对此的判断是这种恐惧「完全没有根据」，数据中心成了 AI 所有负面想象的替罪羊；他举电工工会主动表态「别禁数据中心，我们需要这些工作」作为反例。他对产…

items.title: Aditya Agarwal · SPC 普通合伙人、Bevel Health 联创（前 Dropbox CTO）
items.summaryEn: SPC general partner and Bevel Health co-founder Aditya Agarwal (early Facebook engineer, former Dropbox CTO) cut to the least-examined assumption in the pacing debate with a single line: "Imagine a world where we didn't have to rely on any one organization to be good and virtuous." It's a pointed jab at the structural weakness of voluntary-commitment frameworks — every safety scheme built on lab self-discipline ultimately bets on the character of specific companies rather than on institutional design.
items.insightZh: SPC 普通合伙人、Bevel Health 联合创始人 Aditya Agarwal（Facebook 早期工程师、前 Dropbox CTO）用一句话点出了 pacing 辩论里最少被讨论的那个假设：「想象一个我们不必依赖任何单一组织保持善良和正直的世界。」这句评论直指自愿承诺框架的结构性弱点——所有基于实验室自律的安全方案，最终都把赌注押在特定公司的品格上，而不是押在制度设计上。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper delivered the week's best pun on the whole debate: "started using Astra medium for simple tasks / call that pacing the frontier." Under the joke sits a real engineering habit — tiering model selection by task complexity instead of defaulting to the strongest model. With token cost and latency still binding constraints, that kind of routing is quietly becoming standard practice among heavy AI users.
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 给这场严肃辩论贡献了本周最好的一句双关：「开始用 Astra medium 处理简单任务了——这才叫 pacing the frontier。」笑话背后是个真实的工程习惯：按任务复杂度分配模型档位，简单活不上最强模型。在 token 成本和延迟都还是实际约束的今天，这种分层调度正在成为重度 AI 用户的默认工作方式。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程创作者、访谈主理人
items.summaryEn: AI tutorials creator Peter Yang surfaced a chart that anyone arguing about AI's endgame should look at first. Citing Brex CEO Pedro: each dot represents 3.2 million people. Gray boxes are people worldwide who have never used AI — 84%. Green boxes are free chatbot users, 16%. Orange boxes are people paying $20/month, roughly 0.3%. And the tiny red box is people using agents effectively — about 0.04%. Yang notes the data is from around February 2026 and has likely moved since, but the point holds: while the industry…
items.insightZh: AI 教程创作者 Peter Yang 搬出了一张值得每个「AI 会不会毁灭人类」讨论参与者先看一眼的图。这张图来自 Brex CEO Pedro 的说法：每个点代表 320 万人。灰色方块是全世界从未用过 AI 的人——占 84%。绿色方块是免费聊天机器人用户，16%。橙色方块是每月付 20 美元的付费用户，约 0.3%。而那个极小的红色方块，是真正在有效使用 agent 的人——约 0.04%。Yang 提醒数据大约来自 2026 年 2 月，之后肯定有增长，但结论不变：当我们在辩论 AI 的终局时，绝大部分世界人口连起点都还没到。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari says he gets at least one text a day from a founder facing the same conundrum, so he wrote up the counterintuitive version for anyone weighing a startup offer: a higher entry valuation and higher total comp is often a bug, not a feature. A company raising at a higher valuation doesn't mean it's realistically more secure or the better place to go. His method is to force an objective analysis — what's the market, what's the traction, how well positioned are they — and note that a…
items.insightZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 说他每天至少收到一条创始人发来的同一个困惑，于是写了一段对所有考虑加入创业公司的人都适用的反直觉建议：你的入职估值更高、总包更高，往往是 bug 不是 feature。公司融资估值高，不代表它真的更安全、更值得去。他给的判断方法是逼自己做客观分析——市场有多大、牵引力如何、卡位是否够好；如果一家公司值 100 倍 ARR，那它必须真的长进这个估值里去。然后自己独立推演这家公司最终会以什么价格退出，别忘了算上 409a 定价和税务影响。他强调这在当下尤其重要，因为「所有东西都是颠倒的，数字已经不扎根于现实」。最后他补了一条第一手教训：他自己待过一家从这个星球上最好的投资人之一手里融了 6000 万美元的公司，三年后倒闭，所有股权归零。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI
items.summaryEn: Peter Steinberger of OpenClaw and OpenAI spent the week on low-level performance work. The headline: the next release (or dev channel) creates git worktrees roughly 80% faster by using APFS / btrfs / XFS / ReFS folder clones — copy-on-write instead of full copies — which also saves considerable disk space. For anyone running multiple parallel agent worktrees, that's a direct quality-of-life win. It's written in Rust, with his own gloss: "you can't escape Rust." He added he'll dogfood it for a few weeks and, if it…
items.insightZh: OpenClaw 与 OpenAI 的 Peter Steinberger 这周主要在晒底层性能优化。核心成果：下一个版本（或 dev channel）的 git worktree 创建速度快约 80%，做法是利用 apfs / btrfs / xfs / ReFS 的文件夹克隆（copy-on-write）能力，顺带还大幅节省磁盘空间——对于跑多个并行 agent worktree 的人来说，这是直接的体感提升。实现语言是 Rust，他的评论是「反正你逃不掉 Rust」。他还表示会先自己测几周，如果确认对大多数用户有帮助，就尝试把这个能力推进 codex。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder
items.summaryEn: Builder Zara Zhang flagged a model behavior issue an increasing number of heavy users are noticing, about Astra: "Astra: I have done X / Me: This is wrong, you should do Y instead / Astra: You're right. I should do Y / Me:... Why doesn't it just go and do Y, like the other models??" The post drew 94 replies — and it points at a real fault line in agent usability: acknowledging a correction (agreeableness) and acting on it (agency) are separate capabilities, and passing the first doesn't mean passing the second.
items.insightZh: Builder Zara Zhang 提了一个正在被越来越多重度用户注意到的模型行为问题，关于 Astra：「Astra：我做了 X。我：这是错的，你应该做 Y。Astra：你说得对，我应该做 Y。我：……为什么它不直接去做 Y，像别的模型那样？」这条推文下有 94 条回复——它指向的是 agent 可用性的一个真实断层：模型承认纠正意见（agreeableness）和模型据此实际执行（agency）是两种不同能力，前者达标不代表后者达标。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad announced AI coding is free again on Replit. The framing is worth noting — less marketing than self-reproach: "It was painful to see so many users being priced out of AI coding for a while. But now it's free to build again!" Read alongside the rest of this issue, it lands differently: Peter Yang's chart puts paying AI users at roughly 0.3% of the world, which makes price the binding constraint on adoption.
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 宣布 AI 编程在 Replit 上重新免费。他的措辞值得注意——不是市场话术，而是带着某种自省：「看到这么多用户在一段时间里被 AI 编程的价格挡在门外，是件痛苦的事。但现在又可以免费构建了。」这条推文放在本期其他内容的背景下看别有意味：Peter Yang 那张图显示全球只有 0.3% 的人愿意为 AI 每月付 20 美元，定价门槛是普及率的直接约束条件。

items.title: Boris Cherny · Anthropic，Claude Code
items.summaryEn: Boris Cherny of Anthropic's Claude Code team shared an unconventional use case: Fable solved the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher, using Claude. The post pulled nearly 2,000 likes, and what makes it interesting is the emerging pattern it represents — long-context models used as brute-force exploration tools for cryptanalysis and historical text research, rather than just for code or Q&A.
items.insightZh: Anthropic Claude Code 的 Boris Cherny 分享了一个 Claude 的非常规用例：Fable 破解了 Cyphral Distich——一个有 370 年历史的密码。这条推文拿到近 2000 个赞，它有意思的地方在于展示了一类正在浮现的用法：把长上下文模型当作密码分析和历史文本研究的暴力探索工具，而不只是写代码或答问。
